description: Edit a wiki page: retitle it, change its body, move it under another parent (or to the top of its space), or set its labels. Identify it by 'id', or by 'spaceKey' + 'title'. To change part of the body, pass 'edits' (exact find-and-replace on the Markdown source, each 'oldText' occurring exactly once) or 'replaceSection' — the answer says where each landed, not the page, so a one-line fix to a long page costs one line. Or pass 'operations' — insert, replace, delete or move a block, set a table cell, add or drop a row, set a formula, rename a term, tick a checklist item, retitle — addressed by names that survive other people's edits (a claim's label, an {anchor:…}, a \label, a heading's anchor, a table row by its first cell and a column by its header), with 'baseVersion' the version you read: what others wrote since is merged with yours block by block, and the answer says per operation 'applied', 'merged', 'conflict' or 'gone'. All or nothing unless partial: true. 'markdown' replaces the whole body — read it first with get_wiki_page(withMarkdown: true) and edit that, or the page's links, images and macros are dropped; 'appendMarkdown' adds to the end and leaves what is there untouched. Mention someone as [@Their Name](user:username), the wiki's own form. Requires permission to edit the page. A page with ```anim blocks answers 'anims': per block, whether it plays or every problem with where it stands. Answers with 'notified' (who this actually reaches) and 'unresolvedMentions' (what looked like a mention and reached nobody, each with a reason) — a wrong handle is stored as written and never refused, so that list is the only sign it did not land.

appendMarkdown.description: Markdown to add to the end of the page, leaving the rest as it is. Same syntax as 'markdown'.

baseVersion.description: The version you read (get_wiki_page's 'version') and wrote your change on. Unlike 'expectedVersion', an edit somebody made since is MERGED with yours, block by block, when the two touch different paragraphs, list items, table cells or words; where both changed one place nothing of the call is written and 'conflicts' lists each place (base, mine, current) — unless partial: true. Works with 'operations', 'edits', 'replaceSection', 'newTitle' and a whole 'markdown'. Not with 'expectedVersion'.

edits.description: Exact replacements in the page's Markdown source — the text get_wiki_page returns with 'section', 'offset' or withMarkdown: true. Every 'oldText' is matched against the page as you read it (not against the result of the other edits) and must occur exactly once unless 'replaceAll' is set; if any edit does not fit, none is applied. Pair with 'expectedVersion'.

newText.description: What to put in its place. An empty string deletes. To insert, put an anchor in 'oldText' and the same anchor plus the addition here.

oldText.description: The text to replace, exactly as it stands in the Markdown source — whitespace and line breaks included. Must occur exactly once unless 'replaceAll' is set; include a few surrounding words to make it unique.

replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence rather than requiring exactly one.

expectedVersion.description: The version you read (from get_wiki_page). If the page has moved on since, the edit is refused instead of overwriting someone else's. 'baseVersion' instead merges with what was written since.

labels.description: Labels to set, space or comma separated. Replaces the existing set. Stored in lower case, except a label starting with '$', which is kept exactly as written; list_wiki_labels shows the ones the space already uses.

markdown.description: The complete new body as Markdown — replaces what is there. Carries $…$ / $$…$$ LaTeX formulas and the wiki's macros on a line of their own ({toc}, {children}, {info} … {info}, {expand:title=…} … {expand}). A theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, conjecture or question is a block of its own — ::: theorem {#thm:label status=computer number=5.8 title="…"} on its line, the statement, then ::: — read into the project's register of claims at the save (list_claims); 'claims' in the answer says which.

message.description: Short note for the page history, e.g. why you changed it.

minorEdit.description: Mark this as a minor edit in the history.

newTitle.description: New title. The page's existing links follow the rename.

operations.description: Changes to the body addressed by what survives an edit, applied on 'baseVersion' (default: the version now) and merged with whatever was written since. Each is {op, …}: insert_block {markdown, after|before: <block> | startOf|endOf: <section>; none of them: the end of the body}; replace_block {target: <block>, markdown}; delete_block {target}; move_block {target, after|before|startOf|endOf}; replace_section {section, markdown — heading line included; "" removes it}; replace_text {oldText, newText, replaceAll?, target?: <block> | section?} — exactly once in that scope (default the whole body); set_cell {table?, row|rowIndex, column|columnIndex, value}; insert_row {table?, row|rowIndex (after it; rowIndex 0: first; neither: last), cells[]}; delete_row {table?, row|rowIndex} — 'row' is the row's FIRST cell, 'column' a header, indexes from 1, 'table' left out when the body has one; set_formula {target: a $$ block, or anchor 'label:<\label>' for a formula anywhere, tex}; rename_term {from, to, section?} — whole words only, never inside code, formulas, links, mentions or macros, one block at a time; set_checklist_item {item: id or words, checked}; set_title {title} (pages). A <block> is {anchor} — a claim's label, an {anchor:…} name, a \label, a heading's anchor, or a full key 'claim:…', 'anchor:…', 'label:…', 'h:…', 'check:…' — or {quote: ≥8 characters found in exactly one block}, or {section, index} (1: the first block under the heading, 0: the heading) or {index} alone (the body's n-th block). Optional 'expect' on any operation but rename_term: the target's text as you read it — if it reads otherwise on that version the operation is 'gone'. The answer's 'operations' says per operation 'applied', 'merged' (somebody else changed that block too and both stand), 'conflict' (both changed one word, cell, formula or atomic block — see 'conflicts', each with base, mine and current text) or 'gone' (its address is not on that version, or 'expect' differs). ALL OR NOTHING: one conflict or one gone operation writes nothing — unless partial: true, which writes the rest as one version. Two operations that change the same text, or one that cannot be read, refuse the call.

after.description: insert_block / move_block: put it right after this block.

anchor.description: A name the text gives the block: a claim's label ('thm:main', from ::: theorem {#thm:main}), an {anchor:name} line's name (the block under it), a formula's \label{…}, a heading's anchor, or a checklist item's id. The full keys get_wiki_page's outline uses — 'claim:thm:main', 'anchor:fig1', 'label:eq:energy', 'h:results', 'check:3fa2…' — are taken as they are.

index.description: The block's place: 1 is the first block after the section's heading (0 the heading itself), or without 'section' the first block of the body. Blocks are paragraphs, list items (each one), tables, formulas, code fences, claims, headings.

quote.description: Words quoted from the block, at least 8 characters, found in exactly one block (spaces and line breaks compared as one space).

section.description: With 'index': the section (its anchor or heading text, as get_wiki_page's 'section') whose blocks are counted. Alone, on 'table' or a set_formula target: the one table (formula) in that section.

before.description: insert_block / move_block: put it right before this block.

anchor.description: A name the text gives the block: a claim's label ('thm:main', from ::: theorem {#thm:main}), an {anchor:name} line's name (the block under it), a formula's \label{…}, a heading's anchor, or a checklist item's id. The full keys get_wiki_page's outline uses — 'claim:thm:main', 'anchor:fig1', 'label:eq:energy', 'h:results', 'check:3fa2…' — are taken as they are.

index.description: The block's place: 1 is the first block after the section's heading (0 the heading itself), or without 'section' the first block of the body. Blocks are paragraphs, list items (each one), tables, formulas, code fences, claims, headings.

quote.description: Words quoted from the block, at least 8 characters, found in exactly one block (spaces and line breaks compared as one space).

section.description: With 'index': the section (its anchor or heading text, as get_wiki_page's 'section') whose blocks are counted. Alone, on 'table' or a set_formula target: the one table (formula) in that section.

cells.description: insert_row: the new row's cells, as many as the table has columns.

checked.description: set_checklist_item: true ticks the box, false clears it.

column.description: set_cell: the column whose header reads this.

columnIndex.description: Instead of 'column': the column's number, from 1.

endOf.description: insert_block / move_block: put it last in this section, after its subsections (anchor or heading text). With none of after/before/startOf/endOf, insert_block appends to the end of the body.

expect.description: Optional, every operation but rename_term: the target's text as you read it (or the SHA-256 hex of it with runs of spaces made one, ends trimmed). If the version you name reads otherwise there, the operation is 'gone' rather than applied to something you did not see.

from.description: rename_term: the word or phrase to rename, matched as a whole word, exactly as written (case included).

item.description: set_checklist_item: the item — its id (get_checklist's, or 'check:…') or its words.

markdown.description: insert_block, replace_block: the Markdown of the block(s). replace_section: the section with its heading line; an empty string removes the section.

newText.description: replace_text: what to put in its place (an empty string deletes).

oldText.description: replace_text: the exact text to replace, as the source has it; it must occur exactly once in the scope unless replaceAll.

op.description: What to do: insert_block, replace_block, delete_block, move_block, replace_section, replace_text, set_cell, insert_row, delete_row, set_formula, rename_term, set_checklist_item, set_title.

replaceAll.description: replace_text: replace every occurrence in the scope.

row.description: set_cell, delete_row: the row whose FIRST cell reads this. insert_row: the new row goes after it.

rowIndex.description: Instead of 'row': the row's number, 1 being the first row under the header. insert_row: 0 puts the new row first; leave both out to add it last.

section.description: replace_section: the section (anchor or heading text). replace_text, rename_term: limit the operation to this section.

startOf.description: insert_block / move_block: put it first in this section, right under its heading (anchor or heading text).

table.description: set_cell, insert_row, delete_row: the table. Leave it out when the body has one table; a 'section' alone means the one table in that section.

anchor.description: A name the text gives the block: a claim's label ('thm:main', from ::: theorem {#thm:main}), an {anchor:name} line's name (the block under it), a formula's \label{…}, a heading's anchor, or a checklist item's id. The full keys get_wiki_page's outline uses — 'claim:thm:main', 'anchor:fig1', 'label:eq:energy', 'h:results', 'check:3fa2…' — are taken as they are.

index.description: The block's place: 1 is the first block after the section's heading (0 the heading itself), or without 'section' the first block of the body. Blocks are paragraphs, list items (each one), tables, formulas, code fences, claims, headings.

quote.description: Words quoted from the block, at least 8 characters, found in exactly one block (spaces and line breaks compared as one space).

section.description: With 'index': the section (its anchor or heading text, as get_wiki_page's 'section') whose blocks are counted. Alone, on 'table' or a set_formula target: the one table (formula) in that section.

target.description: The block the operation acts on (replace_block, delete_block, move_block, set_formula; replace_text's scope).

anchor.description: A name the text gives the block: a claim's label ('thm:main', from ::: theorem {#thm:main}), an {anchor:name} line's name (the block under it), a formula's \label{…}, a heading's anchor, or a checklist item's id. The full keys get_wiki_page's outline uses — 'claim:thm:main', 'anchor:fig1', 'label:eq:energy', 'h:results', 'check:3fa2…' — are taken as they are.

index.description: The block's place: 1 is the first block after the section's heading (0 the heading itself), or without 'section' the first block of the body. Blocks are paragraphs, list items (each one), tables, formulas, code fences, claims, headings.

quote.description: Words quoted from the block, at least 8 characters, found in exactly one block (spaces and line breaks compared as one space).

section.description: With 'index': the section (its anchor or heading text, as get_wiki_page's 'section') whose blocks are counted. Alone, on 'table' or a set_formula target: the one table (formula) in that section.

tex.description: set_formula: the new TeX, without the $ or $$ around it.

title.description: set_title: the page's new title (merged as a field). Wiki pages only.

value.description: set_cell: the cell's new text, one line. A '|' must be written \| unless it is inside $…$ or `code`.

parentId.description: Move the page under this parent page id.

parentTitle.description: Move the page under the page with this title, in the same space.

partial.description: With baseVersion or operations: on a conflict, or an operation that is 'gone', write everything else anyway as one version; the answer still lists what was left out. Default false: all or nothing.

replaceSection.description: Replace one whole section: 'section' names it as get_wiki_page's 'section' does (anchor or heading text), 'markdown' is what replaces it — heading line included, as reading the section returned it. Can be combined with 'edits' elsewhere on the page.

markdown.description: The Markdown that replaces it, heading line included — the section as get_wiki_page(section: …) returned it, changed. An empty string removes the section.

section.description: The section to replace: its anchor as get_wiki_page(outline: true) gives it, or its heading text.

spaceKey.description: Space key, when identifying the page by title.

title.description: Current page title, when identifying the page by title.

toTopLevel.description: Move the page to the top of its space, out from under any parent, so it sits beside the space's other root pages. Use this instead of parentId/parentTitle — a tool argument has no way to say 'no parent' by leaving one out.
